metadata.description: Sample datasets with analysis prompts for training data science and ML skills

datasets.name: E-commerce Customer Behavior
datasets.description: Customer transaction and behavior data for churn prediction and segmentation

schema.name: product_categories
schema.description: Number of different categories purchased from

analysis_prompts.prompt: Perform exploratory data analysis on the customer dataset. Identify key patterns, distributions, and correlations.
expected_steps: Check for missing values and data quality issues
Analyze distribution of numerical features (histograms, box plots)
Calculate correlation matrix for numerical features
Examine churn rate and class imbalance
key_insights: High correlation between total_purchases and total_spent (r=0.92)
Churned customers have significantly higher days_since_last_purchase (median: 145 vs 18)
Email engagement is negatively correlated with churn
Support tickets show weak positive correlation with churn

analysis_prompts.prompt: Build a churn prediction model. What features are most important? What accuracy can you achieve?
expected_approach: Split data into train/test (80/20 or cross-validation)
Handle class imbalance (SMOTE, class weights, or stratified sampling)
Try multiple models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost
Evaluate using precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC (not just accuracy)

analysis_prompts.prompt: Segment customers into groups based on their behavior. Describe each segment.
expected_approach: Determine optimal k using elbow method or silhouette score

expected_segments.name: High-Value Loyalists
expected_segments.characteristics: High total_spent, low days_since_last_purchase, high email_engagement

expected_segments.name: At-Risk
expected_segments.characteristics: High days_since_last_purchase, declining engagement, multiple support tickets

expected_segments.name: Bargain Hunters
expected_segments.characteristics: Low avg_order_value, high purchase frequency during sales

expected_segments.name: Occasional Shoppers
expected_segments.characteristics: Moderate spending, low frequency, responsive to seasonal campaigns

datasets.name: Real Estate Prices
datasets.description: Housing price data for regression modeling

analysis_prompts.prompt: Build a price prediction model. What factors most influence house prices?
expected_approach: Feature engineering: age of house (current_year - year_built), price per sqft
Try Linear Regression, Ridge, Lasso, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting

analysis_prompts.prompt: Identify overpriced and underpriced properties based on your model.

datasets.name: Marketing Campaign Performance
datasets.description: Time series data on marketing campaign metrics

analysis_prompts.prompt: Analyze marketing campaign performance over time. Identify trends and seasonality.
expected_approach: Calculate derived metrics: CTR, CPC, Conversion Rate, ROAS
Plot time series with trend lines
Decompose into trend, seasonality, residual (STL decomposition)

analysis_prompts.prompt: Forecast next month's conversions and revenue.
Optimize ad spend allocation across days of week to maximize ROAS.
expected_approach: Calculate ROAS by day of week

datasets.name: Sensor Data - Equipment Maintenance
datasets.description: IoT sensor data for predictive maintenance

analysis_prompts.prompt: Detect anomalies in sensor readings that might indicate impending failure.
expected_approach: Statistical methods: Z-score, IQR for outlier detection
Isolation Forest for multivariate anomaly detection
Set thresholds based on normal operation

analysis_prompts.prompt: Build a model to predict equipment failure 24 hours in advance.
expected_approach: Feature engineering: rolling means, std dev, rate of change
Handle time dependencies with LSTM or lag features
Optimize for recall (catch all potential failures)
Evaluate cost: false positive vs false negative
analysis_prompts.business_impact: Reduce unplanned downtime by 60%, maintenance cost by 30%

datasets.name: Natural Language - Product Reviews
datasets.description: Customer product reviews for sentiment analysis and topic modeling

sample_data.review_text: Absolutely love this product! The quality exceeded my expectations and shipping was fast. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a reliable solution.
Disappointed with the purchase. The product arrived damaged and customer service was unresponsive. Would not buy again.

analysis_prompts.prompt: Perform sentiment analysis on reviews. Does sentiment align with ratings?
expected_approach: Use VADER or TextBlob for rule-based sentiment
TF-IDF or word embeddings as features
Identify reviews where sentiment disagrees with rating

analysis_prompts.prompt: Extract main topics discussed in negative reviews (rating ≤ 2).
expected_approach: Apply LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) for topic modeling
Identify common complaints: shipping, quality, customer service, etc.

data_preprocessing_exercises.scenario: A dataset has 15% missing values in 'income' column, 5% in 'age', and 30% in 'phone_number'.
questions: How would you handle each column differently?
When would you drop rows vs impute?
What imputation strategies are appropriate for each column?

solutions.income: Impute with median (robust to outliers) or use regression imputation based on correlated features
solutions.age: Impute with median or mean (if normally distributed), or mode if discrete age groups
solutions.phone_number: Likely not predictive - consider dropping column or flag as missing (create is_missing indicator)

solution.answer: Yes, scale for distance-based algorithms (KNN, SVM, Neural Networks, K-means)
solution.method: StandardScaler (z-score) if features are approximately normal. MinMaxScaler if bounded ranges preferred. RobustScaler if outliers present.

data_preprocessing_exercises.scenario: Variables: country (200 unique), product_category (5 unique), order_priority (low/medium/high)
data_preprocessing_exercises.question: How to encode each variable?

solutions.country: High cardinality - use target encoding or frequency encoding. One-hot creates too many features (curse of dimensionality)
solutions.order_priority: Ordinal variable - label encode with order: low=0, medium=1, high=2
